items.title: Section: The Three Causes and Fruits Behind a Bodhisattva's Capacity to Help — Eight Marks of Ripening

items.zh: 略說應知三因三果。何等為三？一者、異熟因、異熟果，二者、福因、福果，三者、智因、智果。
items.en: In brief, one should know there are three causes and three fruits. What are the three? First, the cause and fruit of karmic ripening; second, the cause and fruit of merit; third, the cause and fruit of wisdom.

items.zh: 云何異熟？謂略有八。一者、壽量具足；二者、形色具足；三者、族姓具足；四者、自在具足；五者、信言具足，六者、大勢具足，七者、人性具足，八者、大力具足。
items.en: What is karmic ripening? In brief, there are eight kinds: complete longevity; complete fineness of form; complete nobility of birth; complete authority; complete credibility; complete greatness of influence; complete manhood; and complete strength.

items.zh: 若諸菩薩長壽久住，是名菩薩壽量具足。形色端嚴，眾所樂見，顏容殊妙，是名菩薩形色具足。生豪貴家，是名菩薩族姓具足。得大財位、有大朋翼、具大僚屬，是名菩薩自在具足。
眾所信奉，斷訟取則，不行諂誑、偽斗秤等，所受寄物終不差違，於諸有情言無虛妄；以是緣故，凡有所說無不信受，是名菩薩信言具足。
items.en: Trusted and deferred to by all, taken as the standard when settling disputes, never resorting to flattery or deceit, false measures or false scales; anything entrusted to their keeping is never mishandled; their word to any being is never false — for this reason, whatever they say is universally believed. This is called a bodhisattva's completeness of credibility.

items.title: The Remaining Marks of Ripening, and What Actually Produces Each One

items.zh: 有大名稱，流聞世間。所謂具足勇健精進、剛毅、敏捷、審悉善戒，種種伎藝工巧業處，展轉妙解，出過餘人。由此因緣，世所珍敬，為諸大眾供養、恭敬、尊重、讚歎，是名菩薩大勢具足。具丈夫分，成就男根，是名菩薩人性具足。為性少疾，或全無病，有大堪能，是名菩薩大力具足。
items.en: Possessing great renown, spread throughout the world — endowed with courage, diligence, resolve, sharpness, and careful discernment within the wholesome precepts, and surpassing others in every craft and skill … this is called a bodhisattva's completeness of influence … by nature rarely ill, or entirely free of illness, possessing great capability — this is called a bodhisattva's completeness of strength.

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩於諸眾生不加傷害，遠離一切傷害意樂，是名菩薩壽量具足因。惠施光明鮮淨衣物，是名菩薩形色具足因。於諸眾生捨離憍慢，是名菩薩族姓具足因。於資生具有所匱乏遊行乞匃諸眾生所，隨欲惠施，是名菩薩自在具足因。所言誠諦，亦不好習乖離、麁獷不相應語，是名菩薩信言具足因。攝持當來種種功德於自身中，發弘誓願、供養三寶及諸尊長，是名菩薩大勢具足因。樂丈夫體，厭婦女身深見過患。由二因緣，施他人性。一者、女人樂女身者，勸令厭離解脫女身；二者、丈夫將失男根，方便護攝令不失壞，及說正法令得男身。是名菩薩人性具足因。於諸眾生以身供事，隨其所作如法事業皆往營助，如己力能，以其正法，不以卒暴，用能增長身心勢力餅、飯、糜等種種飲食施諸眾生，是名菩薩大力具足因。
items.en: Never harming any being, entirely free of any wish to cause harm — this is the cause of long life … giving light and clean, fresh clothing — this is the cause of fine appearance … relinquishing pride towards every being — this is the cause of noble birth … truthful speech, never divisive or coarse — this is the cause of credibility … gathering merit for the future, raising the great vow, making offerings to the three treasures and one's elders — this is the cause of great influence … personally serving other beings' lawful undertakings … giving nourishing food that strengthens body and mind — this is the cause of great strength.

items.zh: 當知前說八種異熟，以此所說八種為因。

blocks.text: Fascicle 36 finishes the chapter on self-benefit and benefiting others, then opens the **chapter on true meaning** (真實義品), one of the most important philosophical passages in the whole treatise. Today: the qualities a bodhisattva's past actions ripen into, which make helping others possible.
Of karmic ripening, of merit, and of wisdom.

"Complete longevity; fineness of form; nobility of birth; authority; credibility; greatness of influence; manhood; strength." Credibility: "trusted by all, taken as the standard when settling disputes, never using false measures or false scales; anything entrusted is never mishandled; their word is never false". Master Cháng Bǎi tells of an old monk trusted with others' valuables.
"Great renown, spread throughout the world; endowed with courage, diligence, sharpness, and discernment; surpassing others in every craft."

"Never harming any being: the cause of long life. Giving light and clean, fresh clothing: the cause of fine appearance. Relinquishing pride towards every being: the cause of noble birth. Truthful speech:" the cause of credibility; and so on.

Every quality here is valued for one reason: it helps the bodhisattva help others. Long life gives time; credibility makes others listen; strength makes effort possible. Even good fortune is put to work.

quiz.q: "First, the cause and fruit of karmic ripening (異熟)." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain 異熟?
options: the old rendering is "karmic retribution" — the fruit
quiz.why: "What are the three? First, the cause and fruit of karmic ripening; second, the cause and fruit of merit; third, the cause and fruit of wisdom." Venerable Miào Jìng: 異熟 in the old translations is "karmic retribution" — that is, fruit.

quiz.q: "Never resorting to false measures or scales (偽斗稱)." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain?
options: false measures, false scales, and forged documents
quiz.why: "Trusted and deferred to by all, taken as the standard when settling disputes, never resorting to flattery or deceit, false measures or false scales." Master Cháng Bǎi: false measures, false scales, and forged documents — that's "false measures and scales, etc."

quiz.q: Illustrating "never mishandling what is entrusted," both masters tell a story from Tánxū's memoir. The note says the monk was beaten to death. What do the lectures say?
options: Cháng Bǎi: the illiterate monk had no receipt and went to court; Miào Jìng: the official said "no evidence — you slander him!" and had his palms caned
quiz.why: "Anything entrusted to their keeping is never mishandled." Master Cháng Bǎi: the old monk couldn't read and hadn't written a receipt, so, aggrieved, he went to the authorities. Venerable Miào Jìng: "You have no proof — you're slandering him — beat him!" and he was caned on the palms. The note's "beaten to death" doesn't match.

quiz.q: Great influence includes "courage, diligence, resolve (剛毅)." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain 剛毅?
options: once decided, not easily changed or shaken by circumstances
quiz.why: "Endowed with courage, diligence, resolve, and sharpness, keeping the precepts thoroughly." Master Cháng Bǎi: once decided, not easily changed or shaken by outer circumstances — that's 剛毅.

quiz.q: Fine appearance comes from "giving light and clean clothing." How do the masters illustrate "giving light"?
options: Cháng Bǎi: a streetlamp in a dark place for safe passage; Miào Jìng: paying someone's electricity bill
quiz.why: "Giving light and clean, fresh clothing — this is the cause of fine appearance." Master Cháng Bǎi: like placing a streetlamp in a dark spot so passersby walk safely, without fear. Venerable Miào Jìng: if you can't pay your electricity bill, I pay it for you — that's giving you light.
